title_en: JANUS E01 — Newt/Axolotl-Inspired Human Tissue Regeneration: Abstract In-Silico Ablation Study
title_ru: JANUS E01 — синтетические эксперименты по регенерации тканей по принципам тритона с оценкой ограничений для человека

provenance.execution_origin: ChatGPT isolated Python runtime (not GitHub Actions)
provenance.prototype_dataset_note: Digest of a fuller independently generated local JSON containing summaries, paired differences and selected trajectories. Reproduction from the committed script uses a compact result schema, so its JSON bytes will differ; compare numeric summaries and tests, not file hashes.

experiment.randomization: Six per-seed uniform[0.78,1.22] rate multipliers paired across all conditions

metrics.organized_tissue_proxy: Dimensionless 0..1 proxy for organized reconstruction; NOT percentage of human tissue regrowth
metrics.dysregulation_proxy: Dimensionless penalty for dysregulated growth; NOT cancer risk or clinical probability
metrics.sd: Algorithmic between-seed heterogeneity, not experimental uncertainty in humans

findings.claim: The model favors combined control of immune signaling, innervation, positional cues, matrix and progenitor activity over isolated changes.
findings.caveat: Multiplicative interactions were encoded in rate equations before simulation; not a biological discovery.

findings.claim: Under the specified equations, removing nerves or positional signaling strongly reduces the organized reconstruction proxy.
Reducing the artificial growth brake leads to elevated dysregulation index; more apparent reconstruction is not equivalent to safe tissue restoration.

human_translation.relevant_human_evidence: Some distal fingertip injuries exhibit regeneration under defined clinical circumstances; this does not establish adult whole-limb regeneration.
human_translation.next_step: Replace arbitrary rate parameters with separately validated quantitative measurements for a single modest human-relevant context such as skin scarring or fingertip wound dynamics; compare against out-of-sample data.

biology_background.claim: Axolotl macrophages necessary for adult limb regeneration in tested perturbations.
Axolotl positional identity associated with chromatin marks.
Axolotl RA gradient degradation contributes to limb positional identity.
Human fingertip regeneration clinically characterized; not whole-limb regeneration.
Axolotl-derived extracellular matrix investigated in mouse skin wound repair; preclinical.
Axolotl digit regeneration nerve-dependent and requires patterning fidelity.

link_boundary: SkinGPT / SCOBY integration is future exploratory biomaterial sensing research; NO SCOBY tissue-regeneration or wound-healing benefit is claimed.
epistemic_policy: Hypotheses and computations separated from biological evidence. Model self-tests are not independent validation.
future_gates: Recreate numerical results from GitHub-committed Python source and compare paired seed summaries.
Test sensitivity to alternative causal structures, not only rate perturbations.
Calibrate a single-tissue model from accessible experimental data and perform unseen-condition validation.
Freeze success criteria and perform independent computational reproduction before claims of transferable benefit.
